Hello, this place seems nice. Here is a recording of a little circuit bent "rap pad" toy i made for a friend last week.
welcome to the subverse! feel free to tell us more about the ciruit bent toy (pics? schematics? diagrams? written description? etc. etc.) We're here to enjoy and learn!

I just experimented with the original circuit to see what made it do different things. All pretty simple stuff. I added 3 pots, two in place of the resistors in the original circuit. Couple of push button switches that short parts of the circuit and a couple of selector switches all with different sounding results. I also added a bit you can touch with your finger to mess with the sounds even more. Here are some more pics.
Cool shit, do you have a video of the original in action for context?
I do not. Each pad triggered a different beat and more beats when pads were combined. Now I have a working camera I will be sure to more thoroughly document my next build.
Ohhhh. Yea, that sounds like a cool project to fuck with. How technically demanding is the whole circuit bending thing? Are you and engineer?

Personally I reckon circuit bending is piss easy (that's why its so fun). You just need to find some thing that makes a noise, toys are really good, open it up to find the circuit and then start touching it, you can use your fingers or a piece of wire, just experiment by connecting random points in the circuit to see what happens. Make sure to use batteries and not mains power unless your into DIY ECT. A good thing to know is that if there is a resistor in the circuit you can nearly always replace it with a potentiometer, this will often control the speed of the noise. seems like a very interesting field. Most people (including me) regard RF as pure black magic.

RF is pretty magical. I've been in the field about 10 years and I'm still amazed daily.

I'm planning on covering some basics of RF and electromagnetism in the sub. The sub is esoteric but I want to make it approachable.

Sounds very prosing and I'd like to partake if I can.

As a side note I'd like to elaborate on a side effect of platforms like voat and reddit - If the topic is too niche there are very few people taking interest. Since we are talking about a subfield of RF we are talking probably 3 or 4 people at best (I am by no means familiar with the field). So when you create a sub for such a niche topic it tends to create I call "Subverse Isolation" - you know those subs where the only contributors are the two mods and the last post was a year ago. Not a good sight.

I've suffered from that at the other place and once here as well. (/v/openspaceprogram) The solution seems to be to refrain from starting extremely niche subs and keep it under the more general ones until they literally kick you out for spam.

I know this is a really shitty thing to say to someone who just started their niche sub and I'm sorry about that. It just seemed like you might understand what I'm talking about.

I do, I've got the same sub on reddit and only 4 subscribers. It's enough for me to have meaningful discussion about a topic. I'm not really concerned with the number of subscribers. Quality over quantity I suppose.
True, but then you deny the wider public the opportunity to hear about the topic and become interested.
I haven't had a group project in ages, thank god.

I always struggle between wanting to do the whole thing myself just so I don't have to work with other people and not wanting other people to get credit for my work.

I end up doing most of the work.

Ugh. Story time! Back in film school we had this team project where each of us had to come up with an idea and submit it to the rest of the group. At the end, we all had to vote on the project we were going to do as a group. I came up with this short about a person who overdoses on drugs and has this out-of-body experience about where his life was heading and how he was hurting those around him. I can't remember the specifics, but I felt it was pretty creative. Some of the other members of our group came up with some pretty cool ideas too, but you know what the majority of them ended up voting for? A Steve Irwin style video mockumentary about the students at the school, observing them in their "natural habitat". It was every bit as bad as I thought it would be. FML.

The last group project I had to do is college ended like this. In a group of four people in a non-introductory class, I was the only one that actually read the book; no one else even read the spark notes of the book. We were the very last group to present which means that several topics were already covered extensively by other groups. I called a meeting two weeks before a presentation to start working on it, no one showed up. I called a meeting a week before the presentation to start working on it, the other group members came after I hounded them in class and on their phones. Their only contribution was to say that we should literally repeat what the other groups said. I spent an hour arguing with two of them before they agreed to not literally plagiarize, they wanted to 'borrow' the other groups powerpoints. That day ended without any positive headway on the project as the group split up after the argument ended.

Several days of trying to get people to meet up ended with three days before the project was due I had to force the group to meet up to work on the project the next day. I brought ideas about the assignment and we spent two hours this time arguing about copying other groups. The group dissolved without any positive headway on the project again. I spent the next day trying to get the group to meet up again and ended up having to do the whole project by myself the night before it was due this includes a guide for students, a powerpoint and a five page justification for the professor. I even wrote scripts and a one page guide to the book for my group members, e.g. Jon=unfettered capitalism and Mary=communism and why that mattered.

The day of the presentation the group shows up without reading the book, or the guide I made them, and starting rambling about the exact same thing that other groups talked about. During the presentation I had to gentle get my group back on topic several times and present new material all by myself. After about 10 minutes into an hour presentation my group mates got mad at me and stopped talking. I had to give the remaining presentation all by myself with three group members behind me on their phones. Several times during the presentation I tried to get group members to talk about things that I knew they knew because they had talked about it in the class. They would look up from their phone, say a few words and get back to their phone.

After the class ends for the semester I get my grade for that assignment, "B-." The professors comments were roughly, "I liked the ideas presented but they all seemed to have come from AgriGrunt. I am giving AgriGrunt a B- for contributing too much and everyone else an A for the assignment." I cannot tell you want the professor wanted me to do in that situation. That B- resulted in my grade going from an A to an A-.

That sounds like a terrible teacher to me. I'm sorry you had to not only do a presentation basically by yourself but that you got a worse grade because you did more work. Also just the fact that he allowed your teammates to be on their phones during the presentation makes me incredibly angry. That's rude to not just you but the professor as well. Anyways have an up-vote as some small compensation.
